identitySignals: The agenda names the California Department of Social Services, a uniquely named state agency whose official site is cdss.ca.gov (Sacramento).

The Public Health Institute's Center for Immigrant and Refugee Health (CIRH) page on Afghan and Ukrainian refugee students lists CDSS and PHI as partners and a CDSS Office of Immigrant Youth speaker, matching the 'Afghan Refugee School Impact' award funded through the Public Health Institute.
CDSS administers refugee and immigrant youth programs, consistent with OUSD's 'Student health, support & family services' and English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement Office contract.
research.notes: OUSD's agenda lists CDSS as the source of the award, passed through the Public Health Institute (a separate nonprofit, not profiled here). The contact page's email (piar@dss.ca.gov) is the department's public information inbox. CDSS-PHI-ARSI link is corroborated only by the PHI/CIRH news page listing both as partners; the ACF allocation PDF could not be fetched.

profile.summary: The California Department of Social Services is a California state agency that administers social service programs serving more than eight million Californians. These include cash assistance, CalFresh food benefits, In-Home Supportive Services, foster care and child welfare, and community care licensing.

sources.title: Contact Us - California Department of Social Services

review.notes: The agenda names the California Department of Social Services as the funder (passed through the Public Health Institute) for an Afghan Refugee School Impact award; the cited CDSS home and contact pages support the summary (more than eight million people served, CalFresh, IHSS, foster care, licensing, cash assistance), phone, general-inquiries email, address and headquarters. The pass-through link to PHI was not independently confirmed, but the profile correctly describes the agency the agenda names.
